# Prepress Templates: Imposition and Hot Folder Routing

> **⚠️ Imposition templates need in-depth testing before you use them for live jobs.**
> **They haven't yet been fully tested in a working lab, in particular two-sided (duplex) printing and backing up, where each back must line up with its front. Run test jobs on your own press and check the results carefully before sending customer orders. Please report any issues to Pixfizz support.**

**Settings → Prepress** holds the templates that prepare a product before OrderHub Desktop sends it. (Before version 1.19.0 this tab was called **Imposition**.) It has four sections:

| Section | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Paper Sizes** | The press-sheet sizes your imposition templates use. |
| **Imposition Templates** | Step-and-repeat a product's artwork onto press sheets, so the press gets one ready-to-print sheet PDF per job. |
| **Hot Folder Routing** | Send a product straight to a hot folder, unchanged. |
| **Cut Contour Templates** | Make PDFs with a cut line for Onyx and a Graphtec cutter. See the article *Cut Contour Templates: PDFs for Onyx and a Graphtec Cutter*. |

Each template claims one or more **product codes**. A product code can belong to only one Prepress template, in any section.

---

## Step 1: Turn on Prepress templates for the controller

Prepress templates only work on a **PDF Copy** or **Folder Copy** controller with the tick turned on:

1. Go to **Settings → Routing → Order Controllers** and click **Edit** on the PDF Copy or Folder Copy controller.
2. Tick **Apply Prepress templates (Settings → Prepress)**.
3. On a PDF Copy controller, choose **Product with no matching template**:
   * **Write un-imposed to the controller's output folder (today's behaviour)**: products without a template carry on as before.
   * **Write un-imposed to a product-code subfolder**: products without a template land in a folder named after their product code. Choose this if you impose those products by hand.
4. Click **Save Controller**.

* Note: Until you tick it, the controller sends exactly as it always has.
* Note: Other controllers, such as Darkroom Pro, Epson or Fuji, ignore Prepress templates.

---

## Step 2: Add your paper sizes

1. Go to **Settings → Prepress → Paper Sizes** and click **+ Add Paper Size**.
2. Enter a **Name** your team will recognise, for example `12×18 gloss`.
3. Enter the **Width** and **Height**, and pick the **Unit** (**in** or **mm**).
4. Click **Save Paper Size**.

* Note: A paper size can't be deleted while a template uses it. The message names the templates to change first.

---

## Step 3: Build an imposition template

1. Go to **Settings → Prepress → Imposition Templates** and click **+ Add Template**.
2. Fill in the fields below. The **live preview** on the right shows the exact layout the press will get, for example "4 per sheet — unrotated (2×2)".
3. Click **Save Template**.

| Field | What to put |
|---|---|
| **Name** | The product family, for example `Grad card 5×7`. |
| **Paper Size** | One from Step 2. All the sizes below are in that paper's unit. |
| **Finished Size** | The trim size of one finished piece, not the size of the supplied artwork. |
| **Margins** | The sheet edges the press can't print into. |
| **Gutter** | The space between neighbouring pieces. Cutters need some. |
| **Artwork Bleed** | The bleed the artwork carries. Leave at 0 to trust the artwork's own trim. Gutter must be at least twice the bleed. |
| **Auto-rotate to best fit** | Tick it unless you need to keep the paper grain one way. A portrait and a landscape product can then share one template. |
| **Draw crop marks** | Corner marks at every piece, for cutting. |
| **Fill last sheet (prints extra copies rather than leaving blanks)** | On: the last sheet is filled with extra copies. Off: exact counts, with blank spaces. |
| **Output sheets** | **All sheets (press prints the file once)**, or **Single master sheet (press prints IMPQTY copies)** for a proof-then-multiply workflow. |
| **Mode** | **Simplex (one-sided)** or **Duplex (two-sided)**. |
| **Duplex Flip Edge** | **Long edge** or **Short edge**. This must match your press (see below). |
| **Product Codes** | The codes this template handles. |
| **Output Path** | Optional. Blank uses the controller's output path. |
| **Output Subfolder** | Optional. A single folder name, to keep imposed sheets apart from other files. |
| **Place in a job subfolder** | Off by default, so the PDF lands straight in the folder, because press hot folders usually don't look in sub-folders. |
| **Filename Template** | Optional. Blank uses the standard name. |

![Imposition Template](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/f2b0b09f-e43a-4c58-9f4d-951b5323fb2c.png)

### What the press gets

One PDF per job, named like `{order number}_{job id}_QTY20_IMPQTY5.pdf`:

* **QTY** is the copies the customer ordered.
* **IMPQTY** is the number of sheets, which is the run length to set on the press.

For example, 20 copies of a 5×7 card at 4 per sheet give `QTY20_IMPQTY5`: 5 sheets.

* Note: Imposition takes PDF, JPEG and PNG artwork. RGB only: a CMYK JPEG is refused, with a message telling you to save it as RGB.
* Note: Images are stretched to fill each piece, so supply artwork in the right shape for the finished size.

---

## Duplex: check the flip edge once

> **Test this before live jobs.** Backing up hasn't been fully tested in a lab yet. Report any problems to Pixfizz support.

For two-sided templates, **Duplex Flip Edge** must match how your press turns the sheet. If it's wrong, every back prints behind the wrong front.

1. Make a duplex template with **Draw crop marks** ticked.
2. Send a small test job, 4 or 8 copies.
3. Trim the sheet and check each back belongs to its front.
4. If not, switch **Duplex Flip Edge** between **Long edge** and **Short edge** and try again.

Once it's right for a press, use the same setting on every duplex template for that press.

---

## Hot Folder Routing

Use this when a product should go straight to a hot folder, unchanged, for example when the press or RIP imposes it itself.

1. Go to **Settings → Prepress → Hot Folder Routing** and click **+ Add Hot Folder Route**.
2. Enter a **Name** and the **Product Codes**.
3. In **Output Path**, choose the hot folder. Blank uses the controller's output path.
4. Optional: set a **Filename Template**. Blank keeps each file's own name.
5. Optional: set **Imposed QTY**, which is how many up your press template imposes. It's needed only if the file name uses `{impQty}`.
6. Click **Save Hot Folder Route**.

![Hot Folder Route](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/76b6d7ee-08d5-43ed-a5ee-40ad1cd5665a.png)

* Note: On a **PDF Copy** controller only the job's PDFs are sent. On a **Folder Copy** controller every file is sent.
* Note: Files land straight in the folder. A file already there is never replaced; the new one gets **_2**.
* Note: Before 1.19.0 these were imposition templates with the "pass-through" tick. Yours have moved here by themselves, unchanged.

---

## Good to know

* **Jobs go In Production when they're sent.** Complete them in OrderHub once they're printed.
* **Reprints use the template too.** Imposed reprints end **_R1**, **_R2** and so on.
* **On a Folder Copy controller,** a job sent to an imposition template that holds a file it can't use, such as a TIFF, isn't sent at all. The job shows which file to convert.
* **A job that lands un-imposed** has no template claiming its product code. Check the code in Job Review against your templates. Capital letters and spaces at either end don't matter.
